data.cultural_impact: Deepavali is a major Hindu festival that is celebrated with great fervor and enthusiasm in various parts of India and around the world, particularly by those of Indian origin. The festival is known for its vibrant celebrations includes adorning homes with beautiful decorations, lighting oil lamps called 'diyas', bursting colorful firecrackers, and sharing sweets with loved ones. Deepavali holds immense cultural significance, as it marks the return of Lord Rama to his kingdom after defeating the demon king Ravana. It also commemorates the victory of Goddess Lakshmi, the goddess of prosperity and wealth, and the God Vishnu, the preserver of the universe.
data.spiritual_significance: Deepavali carries deep spiritual significance, as it is believed that the festival symbolizes the triumph of light over darkness. This spiritual theme is expressed through lighting Diwali lamps or 'diyas' and decorating homes with earthenware, clay lamps and candles, signifying the victory of good over evil. The act of meditation, spiritual contemplation, and the sharing of sweets (representing the sweetness of spiritual purity) are integral to the festival's religious observances. The five-day celebration of Diwali also expresses other spiritual themes, such as forgiveness, kindness, and the renewal of relationships. Overall, Deepavali is a time for celebrating spiritual growth and personal victories, while also strengthening bonds with family and friends.

historical_references.reference: Deepavali is also known as the 'Festival of Lights'. It is celebrated in honor of the god Rama returning to his kingdom of Ayodhya after defeating Ravana in the epic battle of Ramayana. This day marks the victory of light over darkness and good over evil.

Another legend associates Deepavali with the return of the god Vishnu, in the form of the god Krishna, to his kingdom of Dwarka after defeating the demon Narakasura. This day marks the victory of Krishna over the demon and the triumph of good over evil.

modern_usage.modern_context: Deepavali, also known as Diwali or the Festival of Lights, is an important Hindu holiday celebrated in India and other countries. It symbolizes the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. In the modern context, Deepavali is seen as a time for family gatherings, feasting, gift-giving, and decorating homes with diyas (oil lamps) and colorful rangoli designs.
